newsitem.title: USA: PhyMatrix to merge with Clinical Studies.
newsitem.headline: PhyMatrix to merge with Clinical Studies.

text.p: PhyMatrix Corp said Wednesday it has signed a binding letter of intent to merge with Clinical Studies Ltd.
The merger will be accounted for as a pooling of interest, PhyMatrix said in an announcement.

Major terms of the deal have been agreed to, said PhyMatrix chief financial officer Fred Leathers, who added that the value of the transaction would be disclosed "when we reach final agreement." Phymatrix, which provides management services to disease specialty and primary care physicians, will be the surviving entity in the merger, Leathers said.

Clinical Studies, which is based in Providence, R.I., is a seven-year-old company that provides independent clinical trials for biopharmaceutical products. It organizes and manages multisite clinical investigators and is among the largest site management organizations in the business, PhyMatrix said.
Clinical Studies has helped over 100 sponsors to move their products through the clinical trial process quickly and efficiently, it added.
Abraham Gosman, chief executive officer and president of PhyMatrix, noted that site management organizations are now only beginning to consolidate the fragmented clinical investigator market.
With the merger, PhyMatrix will provide Clinical Studies access to a broad array of physicians and patients, a key ingredient to success in clinical research, he said.

For the year ended January 31, PhyMatrix had a net income of $12.057 million, versus a net loss of $11.025 million for the year ended December 31, 1995. Net revenues rose to $189.961 million from $70.7 million.
